                   GAINER FAMILY’S REPLY TO EXCEPTIONS

       COME NOW, Franklin and Jane Gainer, Sally Guitar, and Matthew and Mindy

Gainer (collectively, the “Gainer Family”) and file this Reply to Exceptions in the above-

captioned proceeding in accordance with 16 Texas Administrative Code (“TAC”) § 22.261(d).

The Gainer Family respectfully show as follows:

                                      INTRODUCTION

       The Gainer Family, through this Reply to Exceptions, advocates for the denial of the

Application and, if necessary, adoption of Route 894 as the “best meets” route in this proceeding

as proposed by the Administrative Law Judges. In that regard, the Gainer Family adopts and

incorporates by reference here the Reply to Exceptions filed by the G6 Landowners Legal Fund,

LLC. The Gainer Family respectfully suggests that the ALJs consider reviewing the Reply to




                                                   1
 Exceptions filed by the G6 Landowners Legal Fund, LLC, in advance of and in conjunction with

their review of this Reply to Exceptions.

           The Gainer Family is also opposed to the adoption of Route 487 as the “best meets” route,

This Reply to Exceptions is directed at responding to issues and arguments regarding that route.

          The evidentiary record demonstrates that Route 894, as proposed by the Applicants, best

complies with the statutory and regulatory factors that govern this proceeding and should be

recommended by the ALJs and adopted by the Commission. The Gainer Family respectfully

requests that the ALJs make no substantive changes to their PFD and that the Commission adopt

it as written.

          The Gainer Family shows as follows:

                           I. ROUTE 487 IS INFERIOR TO ROUTE 894

          The ALJs considered Route 487 as a “Focus Route” but correctly concluded that Route 894

was a superior route to Route 487. The ALJs correctly found that Routes 487 and 894 achieve

prudent avoidance more effectively than Routes 296 and 392 and that Route 487 has the largest

impact on parks and recreational areas of the Focus Routes.1 The ALJs found Route 487 is the only

Focus Route that runs within 1,000 feet of a park or recreational area and has substantially more

miles within the half-mile foreground visual zone of park and recreational areas.2 In fact, Route

487 runs adjacent to and parallel to Colorado State Bend Park, as depicted on page 119 of the PDF.

           The ALJs noted that no part of Route 894’s centerline runs within 1,000 feet of the parks

or recreational areas or is within the half-mile foreground visual zone of park and recreational




1
    PFD, at 147-148.
2
    PFD, at 148.

                                                   2
 areas.3 The ALJs concluded Route 894 performs favorably when compared to Route 487 on

habitable structures, paralleling existing compatible ROW, crossing rangeland pasture, and

crossing riparian areas.4


        The Gainer Family agrees that Route 487 is inferior to Route 894. Route 487 has 11 more

habitable structures;5 and runs within 100 feet of the north boundary of Colorado Bend State Park. 6

Route 487 performs particularly poorly on other environmental factors as well.

        The PUC Staff advocates for Route 487 and criticizes the PFD for giving “undue weight

to Route 894’s 1-mile distance from Colorado Bend State Park as a distinguishing factor to

recommend the selection of Route 894 over Route 487.” 7 The argument minimizes the extent of

the difference between the two Routes – Route 487 is within 100 feet of the park, while, by PUC

Staff’s admission, Route 894 is a mile away from the park. Intervenor Cherokee Creek Partners

noted, “Route 487, for its part, runs Segment J11 roughly 100 feet from Colorado Bend State Park’s

northern boundary and crosses Colorado Park Road so that park visitors pass directly under the

line.” 8 This difference merits significant weight and supports the ALJs’ recommendation.


        The PUC Staff then highlights Route 487’s overall performance on environmental

integrity, 9 but fails to acknowledge its particularly poor performance on crossing riparian areas

and potential wetlands. Route 487 crosses 271,429 feet of riparian areas, performing 127th of the




3
  PFD, at 148.
4
  PFD, at148.
5
  Application, Table 7-2 from Appendix E of the Environmental Assessment and Alternative Route Analysis; see also
PUC Staff Ex.1, Attachments JP-5 and JP-7; Poole Direct Testimony, Interchange Filing No. 5029, at 60:9-61.
6
  Poole Direct Testimony, Interchange Filing No. 5029, at 40:18.
7
  PUC Staff Exceptions, at 14.
8
  Cherokee Creek Partners Exceptions, at 12, citing Oncor & LCRA TSC Ex. 1, at 249-250.
9
  PUC Staff Exceptions, at 14.

                                                       3
 132 routes Mr. Poole reviewed. 10 Route 487 crosses potential wetlands for 11,471 feet of its length,

ranking 105th of the 132 routes Mr. Poole reviewed.11


        PUC Staff then cites cost as a factor that should weigh in Route 475’s favor, but Mr. Poole

confirmed that all of the proposed routes fall in a “tight range” and that cost differences within his

10 percent rule of thumb lack material significance.12 The ALJs appropriately agreed with Mr.

Poole and correctly “did not find cost to be a distinguishing factor in selecting a route, since the

range of costs for the routes was in a relatively tight range.” 13 The ALJs did not “overlook” the

cost differences between the two routes; they just determined them not to have material

significance, just as Mr. Poole had concluded.


        Finally, PUC Staff asserted, “[T]he PFD does not give total length and paralleling due

weight….” 14 However, the ALJs did weigh the factor and concluded the lengths of the Focus

Routes were comparable. Route 894 is 1.67 miles longer than Route 487.15 The ALJs correctly

determined that, for a project that will range between 214 and 244 miles, that difference was

immaterial. Similarly, the ALJs correctly concluded that a 12-mile difference in paralleling was

not a material difference sufficient to overcome Route 487’s weaknesses.


        Route 894 is the superior route compared to Route 487 and all of the other routes proposed

by the Applicants. Specifically, Route 894 performs better than Route 487 on prudent avoidance

by affecting 11 fewer habitable structures and by being located 1 mile from Colorado Bend State

   Poole Direct Testimony, Interchange No. 5029, at 45:13-14.
11
   Id., at 45:16–18.
12
   Poole, Transcript, Vol. IV at 133-134.
13
   PFD, at 147.
14
   PUC Staff Exceptions, at 18.
15

                                                       4
 Park. Route 487’s location within 100 feet of Colorado Bend State Park is simply unacceptable.

Route 894 also performs significantly better than Route 487 on environmental integrity criteria.

                                          II. PRAYER

       The Gainer Family appreciates the consideration of these issues. Based on the foregoing,

G6 Landowners Legal Fund, LLC respectfully requests that no changes be made to the Proposal

for Decision; and that the Commission deny the Application or, in the alternative, adopt the

Administrative Law Judges’ recommendation that Route 894 be determined the “best meets” route

for this proceeding.

                                             Respectfully submitted,
